# E4 — the fast refresh: can the profile be refreshed without running the program again, and can the model's own report of the dependences close what that leaves open?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

After the model has rewritten a loop, the agent profiles the whole program again; the fast refresh compiles only and carries the last run's dependences over, so the code the model just wrote has no measurement. Does that change whether the agent keeps a rewrite (H6's second half), does the model's own report of the dependences of its new lines repair it (H7), is adding dependences safe where deleting them is not (H7b) — and how many seconds does one refresh save where the run is long? In four steps, the cheap ones first (the author, 12 Oct): (1) the saved rewrites of the model replayed without a model, (2) the model's report on the rewrites that differ, (3) the time on programs with a long run, (4) live trials only if steps 1 and 2 say the refresh keeps DiscoPoP's verdicts. (RQ6, RQ7, C3)

## Result in one paragraph

Step 1 is running since 12 Oct (no model): 599 of the 601 pragma-free rewrites that passed the checks in the trials of E1-v6, E3 and E3b (the setups in which DiscoPoP writes the directive) are replayed on the server — the agent's own verdict and the safety half of its judgement after a fast refresh and after a full re-profile, with a second full re-profile as the control. Known before it: on the 18 loops the run the fast refresh skips is 0.17 s, 0.08 % of the agent's time.

| 2026-10-12 | plan | **E4, step 1 pre-registered — the fast refresh on the model's own rewrites, replayed without a model. Written before any counted replay; registered as group E4, run `e4_replay`.** **What it is.** For every pragma-free rewrite that passed the checks in the archived trials of the setups in which DiscoPoP writes the directive, the program before the rewrite is profiled in full and the rewritten program is then judged twice with the agent's own functions, in the trial's own configuration (its archived command line): after a fast refresh from the profile before the rewrite (`_reprofil_fast`, as phase A calls it) and after a full re-profile (`_reprofil`), each followed by what phase A does next — the runtimes re-measured, the regions rebuilt, DiscoPoP's verdict on the rewritten lines (`_verify_rewrite`, `validate_patterns=False`: `exposed`, `no_pattern`, `no_usable_pragma`) and, where it is `exposed`, the safety half of the judgement of the rewrite as it would ship (`judge_as_shipped`, `measure=None`: `safe_deferred` or `pattern_broken`). Tool `tools/refresh_replay.py`; read-out `results/E04_fast_refresh/analysis/e4_replay_readout.py`. No model; speed is not measured. **The population, fixed:** the `phase: "A"`, `passed` records of the registered runs — E3's `default_v5` on the 18 loops (`e3_r_1` to `e3_r_4`: 227 rewrites) and on the recurrence loops (`e3_d_1` to `e3_d_4`: 52), E3b's `default_v5` (`e3b_1` to `e3b_4`: 144), E1-v6's `default_v4` (`e1v6_r_1` to `e1v6_r_4`: 178) — 601 rewrites in 227 trials, every one free of directives (checked: none is marked as carrying the model's own directive and no diff adds a `#pragma omp` line). The program before each is rebuilt from the trial's own files (the original and the rewrites the trial kept, in order): 599 can be rebuilt, 598 on the original and one on a kept rewrite; two diffs of E1-v6 apply to no state of their trial and are left out, named in the read-out. The correction runs (`e3bc_s316`, `e3c_v8_s341`, the `e1v6c_*` runs) are not in the population; `e3bc_s316`'s rewrites were used to test the tool. **The two units.** (a) *The verdict:* what DiscoPoP says about the rewritten lines — the same after both, parallel only after the fast refresh, parallel only after the full re-profile, or parallel after both with other loops or other directives. (b) *The decision* — the unit of the registered hypotheses, 'decisions that differ from a full re-profile': whether the rewrite would be kept, speed aside — kept after both with the same directives, reverted after both, kept only after the full re-profile, kept only after the fast refresh, or kept after both with other directives. A fast refresh that reports itself unusable is counted apart: the agent then profiles in full. So is a rewrite whose directives the judgement cannot stage: the agent keeps it and leaves the question to its final annotation, which is neither of the two outcomes compared. **The control.** On each rewrite the full re-profile is taken a second time and judged the same way; what differs between the two full re-profiles is what one program's profile differs in from run to run, and the fast refresh's differences are read against it. **What is tested: E4-1.** H6's second half ('the fast refresh saves time without changing decisions'; refuted by 'decisions that differ under fast refresh') on (b): per loop, with the rewrites of all four parts pooled, the share of rewrites whose decision differs after the fast refresh against the share that differs in the control — one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over the loops (29 loops; `main_comparison_stats.wilcoxon_greater`, no test below six non-zero pairs). A new member of the campaign's family: the bound is p × 54. Refuted if the fast refresh changes the decision on more loops' rewrites than the control does; the counts are given beside the p. The time half of H6 is step 3's; the seconds of each refresh are recorded here for these programs. H7 and H7b are step 2's, on the rewrites this step finds different. **Expected, written now** — after the tool's tests on rewrites outside the population and three rewrites of one trial of the population (`e3b_1`, `s314`, repeat 1, replayed on the Mac while the tool was built, verdicts only): the fast refresh makes DiscoPoP report nearly every rewritten loop as freely parallel, because the code the rewrite created has no observed dependence — in the tests a plain `parallel for` where the full profile gives a reduction, and directives on the repetition loop and on inner loops. So (a) differs in most rewrites in which either says parallel. For (b): the gate refuses most of the extra directives, so most decisions are the same; decisions that differ are expected mainly as 'kept only after the full re-profile' — a reduction that the fast refresh turns into a plain `parallel for`, which the checks refuse — in a number I do not predict beyond 'more than a few'; 'kept only after the fast refresh' is expected rare. If (b) differs nowhere, H6's second half stands on these loops and step 2 has nothing to repair; that would surprise me and would be reported as it is. **Read-outs fixed now:** the two tables per experiment and per loop; the statuses crossed; the loops with a directive only after one of the two; the gate's verdicts on the directives of each; what becomes of the rewrites the trials themselves kept; the control beside each count; the test; the agreement with the trials' logged verdicts; the seconds. **Limits, said before the run.** The decision's speed half is not replayed; the judgement is made on one profile of each program; the live agent would continue differently after a different decision, which a replay does not show (step 4 is for that); the trials' rewrites were written by a model that had been told what the FULL profile said about its earlier attempts. **Where and how long:** the server, the DiscoPoP with B23 and B24 repaired, four 12-core groups (parts `e3_r`, `e3_d`, `e3b`, `e1v6` in the folder of `e4_replay`), after the regression of B24 is read; about 40 s a rewrite on the Mac with the gate and before the control was added, so about two to three hours. Step 2 (model calls) starts only after its exact cost has been put to the author. | Plan, E4 step 1 pre-registration |
